key_insight: An E(3)-equivariant diffusion model predicts Wannier centres and their spatial localization, linking atomic structure to electronic polarization and response.
engineering_relevance: The framework could enable scalable screening and finite-temperature simulations of insulating materials for dielectric and piezoelectric applications.
method: Use E(3)-equivariant graph neural networks within a diffusion model.
Predict position-operator moments describing Wannier centres and localization.
Use predicted centres to compute infrared spectra and finite-difference response tensors.
evidence_signal: Demonstrations cover liquid water, amorphous silicon and crystalline BaTiO3, with a universal model generalizing to 100 unseen crystals across a 67-species chemical space.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error metrics, leaving application-specific accuracy—especially for finite-difference response tensors—to be assessed.
paper_title: A Universal Diffusion Model for the Quantum Position Operator
